candidates.label: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif
candidates.support: Wikidata's point for the Temple Mount is corroborated by scholarly archaeological reconstruction of the platform published by Ritmeyer; as a roughly 15-hectare platform, any single point is a center reference rather than a precise boundary.

summary.text: The Temple Mount is the raised platform on Jerusalem's eastern ridge that Herod the Great built up to carry his expanded Second Temple, the center of Jewish worship in the first century AD. Herod began the rebuilding around 20-19 BC; Josephus says the priests finished the temple building itself in about a year and a half and the surrounding cloisters and courts in about eight years, but work on the wider precinct continued for decades, employing over eighteen thousand workers, and was only finished in the early 60s AD. Cloisters ringed the finished precinct for about six furlongs (roughly 1.2 km), and the Antonia fortress, a Roman garrison post, stood at its northwest corner. In John's Gospel, Jesus' own hearers say the Temple "took forty-six years to build," reflecting this long, still-ongoing project.

history.text: The Gospels describe Jesus visiting the Temple as a boy, found sitting among its teachers, and later teaching in its courts and driving out the merchants and money changers who sold sacrificial animals and exchanged coins there. Acts describes the early church continuing to meet at the Temple, including Peter and John healing a man at a gate called Beautiful, and Paul later arrested there by a crowd. These episodes are a sample of the Gospels' and Acts' many references to "the temple," a phrase recurring well over a hundred times in the New Testament.

The Temple was destroyed by Roman forces under Titus in AD 70, ending the sacrificial worship it had hosted; its retaining walls, including the section known today as the Western Wall, survived as its most substantial remains.

Today the platform, also known as Haram al-Sharif, carries the Dome of the Rock and the Al-Aqsa Mosque, both built centuries after the Herodian Temple and outside this project's scope; below it, the Western Wall remains one of Judaism's holiest sites of prayer.

scripture.textWEB: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.
Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

A certain man who was lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, whom they laid daily at the door of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask gifts for the needy of those who entered into the temple.
When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?”
